findings.title: Flex conversion breaks right-aligned small-action button
findings.body: Making .small-action a flex container makes its direct children flex items, and floats do not apply to flex items. The button rule at lines 306-310 still relies on float: right, with no margin-left: auto, justify-content, or other flex positioning to replace it. A small-action delete button will therefore sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge of the post row.

findings.title: order mixin mistranslates values for legacy box ordinal groups
findings.body: The mixin copies $val directly to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, but legacy ordinal groups are 1-based (initial value 1 and values below 1 are invalid) while flex order is 0-based (initial value 0). Consequently order(0) emits an invalid legacy declaration and the legacy translation does not faithfully represent the standard value; the legacy properties should use $val + 1.

findings.title: align-items mixin passes incompatible values to legacy alignment properties
findings.body: The mixin passes $alignment unchanged to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, but those legacy properties accept start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end, so a caller using the standard align-items value flex-start or flex-end will get invalid legacy declarations and lose alignment in the prefixed browsers this mixin targets. It also emits -ms-align-items, which is not the IE10 property. The mixin should translate flex-start/flex-end to start/end for the legacy properties. Current callers use center and baseline, which happen to be spelled the same in both syntaxes.
